title: Adjective Endings Across Cases
subtitle: Stop guessing '-e, -en, -er, -es'—use the Signal Rule to nail adjective endings in seconds.

cheatSheet.summary: Adjective endings aren't random! German wants ONE clear gender/case signal before the noun. If the article already carries the signal (der, dem, den), the adjective relaxes to '-e' or '-en'. If the article doesn't (ein, mein, or no article), the adjective carries the signal itself!
keyTakeaways: After definite articles (der/die/das): ONLY '-e' or '-en'! Use '-e' in Nominative singular (der gute, die gute, das gute) and Accusative F/N. Everywhere else (all Dative, Genitive, Plural, Masculine Akk): '-en'!

After ein/kein/mein: Only 3 slots lack a signal—Nom [M] ('ein guter Mann'), Nom [N] ('ein gutes Buch'), Akk [N] ('ein gutes Buch'). Everywhere else behaves just like definite articles ('-e' or '-en')!
With NO article (Strong): The adjective steals the definite article's ending (kaltes Wasser, frischer Kaffee, mit gutem Wein).
cheatSheet.watchOut: Plural ALWAYS takes '-en' after ANY article (die, meine, keine, alle): 'die neuen Schuhe', 'meine guten Freunde'!

nouns.caseTrigger: 'ein' has no gender ending → adjective must show Masculine '-er'

exercises.rulePill: 'ein' doesn't reveal Masculine [M] gender, so the adjective picks up the '-er' signal from 'der': 'ein toller Vorschlag'.

exercises.english: Today I am wearing my warm coat.
exercises.fullGerman: Ich trage heute meinen warmen Mantel.
exercises.rulePill: Masculine [M] Accusative ALWAYS takes '-en' on the adjective: 'den/einen/meinen warmen Mantel'.

exercises.prompt: Sie wohnt in einer ___ Wohnung im Zentrum.
exercises.english: She lives in a bright apartment in the center.
exercises.fullGerman: Sie wohnt in einer hellen Wohnung im Zentrum.

nouns.caseTrigger: Static location (Wo?) → Dative after 'einer' ALWAYS takes '-en'

exercises.rulePill: Golden shortcut: After ANY article in the Dative (dem, der, einem, einer), the adjective ALWAYS ends in '-en'!

exercises.prompt: Wir kaufen ein ___ Fahrrad für unseren Sohn.
exercises.english: We are buying a blue bicycle for our son.
exercises.fullGerman: Wir kaufen ein blaues Fahrrad für unseren Sohn.

nouns.caseTrigger: 'ein' lacks Neuter signal → adjective takes '-es' from 'das'

exercises.rulePill: 'ein' has no Neuter [N] ending in Nominative or Accusative, so the adjective shows '-es': 'ein blaues Fahrrad'.

exercises.prompt: Zum Frühstück trinke ich gern ___ Kaffee.
exercises.english: For breakfast I like drinking fresh coffee.
exercises.fullGerman: Zum Frühstück trinke ich gern frischen Kaffee.
exercises.rulePill: With no article, the adjective copies the definite article ending directly: Accusative [M] 'den' → 'frischen Kaffee'.

exercises.promptHint: Check the plural adjective ending after 'die'!
exercises.english: The new neighbors are very friendly.
exercises.fullGerman: Die neuen Nachbarn sind sehr freundlich.
exercises.rulePill: After 'die', 'meine', or 'keine' in Plural [PL], the adjective ALWAYS ends in '-en': 'Die neuen Nachbarn'.

exercises.prompt: Der ___ Zug fährt pünktlich um acht Uhr ab.
exercises.english: The fast train departs on time at eight o'clock.
exercises.fullGerman: Der schnelle Zug fährt pünktlich um acht Uhr ab.

nouns.caseTrigger: 'der' ALREADY carries the '-er' signal → adjective takes '-e'

exercises.rulePill: Because 'der' already displays the Masculine [M] '-er' signal, the adjective relaxes to '-e': 'Der schnelle Zug'.

exercises.promptHint: No article before 'Wasser'—what signal does Neuter Nominative need?
exercises.english: Cold water refreshes immediately in summer.
exercises.fullGerman: Kaltes Wasser erfrischt im Sommer sofort.
exercises.rulePill: Without an article, Neuter [N] 'das Wasser' passes its '-s' ending directly onto the adjective: 'Kaltes Wasser'.

exercises.prompt: Er serviert die Suppe mit ___ Brot.
exercises.english: He serves the soup with fresh bread.
exercises.fullGerman: Er serviert die Suppe mit frischem Brot.

nouns.caseTrigger: 'mit' triggers Dative + no article → adjective copies 'dem' → '-em'

exercises.rulePill: 'mit' triggers Dative and there is no article → Neuter [N] 'dem' transfers '-em' onto the adjective: 'mit frischem Brot'.
